problem: Find the parametric equations of the line $\frac{x-11}{-4}=\frac{y+3}{5}=\frac{z+1}{3}.$

activity_context.topic_title: The Cartesian Equation of a Line

feedback.problem: Consider the straight line with the canonical equation $\frac{x-3}{2}=\frac{y-1}{1}=\frac{z+4}{3}.$ Find the vector equation of the line.
feedback.worked_solution:
Remember that the Cartesian (canonical) equation of the straight line that passes through the point $P({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ and is parallel to the vector $v=⟨{v}_{x},{v}_{y},{v}_{z}⟩$, is given by

$$
\frac{x-{x}_{0}}{{v}_{x}}=\frac{y-{y}_{0}}{{v}_{y}}=\frac{z-{z}_{0}}{{v}_{z}}=t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Comparing the above to our given equation

$$
\frac{x-3}{2}=\frac{y-1}{1}=\frac{z-(-4)}{3},
$$

we find that our line passes through the point $P(3,1,-4)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨2,1,3⟩.$ Therefore, its vector equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -4\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
